items.question: What becomes dear to the yoginis through enjoyment, liberation, and great accomplishment?
premises: bhukti mukti mahā siddhiḥ yoginīnāṃ priyo bhavet
the verse links enjoyment liberation and great accomplishment
the result is becoming dear to yoginis
items.inference: The practitioner who attains these becomes dear to the yoginis.
uncertainties: exact syntactic relation of mahā to siddhiḥ
items.plain_english: Enjoyment, liberation, and great accomplishment make one dear to the yoginis.

items.question: Which chapter emerges after candra-dvipa in this sequence?
premises: candra dvīpa vinirgate navamaḥ paṭalaḥ
the ninth chapter emerges from candra-dvipa
the verse names the chapter
items.inference: The ninth chapter is the one that emerges.
uncertainties: whether vinirgate modifies dvīpa or paṭalaḥ
items.plain_english: The ninth chapter emerges from candra-dvipa.

items.question: How is the self described as standing in this fiery image?
premises: vahni nāveṣṭita ātmānam eka pādena saṃsthitam
the self is surrounded by fire
it stands on one foot
items.inference: The self stands on one foot while surrounded by fire.
uncertainties: exact compound parsing of nāveṣṭita
items.plain_english: The self, surrounded by fire, stands on one foot.

items.question: What has been made manifest to the speaker today?
premises: jñānasya nirṇayam deva adya me prakaṭīkṛtam
the determination of knowledge is made manifest
it is addressed to god and given to me
items.inference: The determination of knowledge has been made manifest to the speaker today.
uncertainties: whether deva is vocative or nominative
items.plain_english: Today the determination of knowledge has been made manifest to me, O god.

items.question: How is the eightfold division to be known?
premises: aṣṭa aṣṭaka vibhāgam tu parijñātum anantathā
the eightfold division is to be known fully
it is endless in manner
items.inference: The eightfold division is to be known fully and endlessly.
uncertainties: exact relation of aṣṭa and aṣṭaka
items.plain_english: The eightfold division is to be known fully, endlessly.

items.question: How does the secret place or wheel become accomplished quickly?
premises: guhya sthānaṃ yathā cakraṃ kṣipraṃ sidhyati bhairava
the secret place is like a wheel
it is accomplished quickly
items.inference: The secret place or wheel is accomplished quickly, O Bhairava.
uncertainties: whether guhya modifies sthānaṃ or cakraṃ
items.plain_english: As the secret place is like a wheel, it is quickly accomplished, O Bhairava.

items.question: What is said to be hard to obtain even by gods?
premises: sādhu sādhu mahādevi pṛṣṭaḥ aham sura durlabham
the speaker was asked by the great goddess
the matter is hard to obtain by gods
items.inference: The teaching or attainment discussed is hard to obtain even by gods.
uncertainties: exact referent of durlabham
items.plain_english: Well, well, O great goddess, I was asked; it is hard to obtain even by gods.

items.question: Where are the syllables kṣa and laṃ placed in this mapping?
premises: kṣakāraṃ brahmarandhratvaṃ laṃkāram tu lalāṭayoḥ
kṣa is linked with brahmarandhra
laṃ is linked with the forehead
items.inference: The syllables are mapped to brahmarandhra and the forehead.
uncertainties: whether brahmarandhratvaṃ is locative sense
items.plain_english: The syllable kṣa is brahmarandhra, and the syllable laṃ is in the forehead.

items.question: Where are the syllables ṣa and śa placed in this mapping?
premises: ṣakāraṃ kaṇṭha deśe tu śakāraṃ hṛdaye tadā
ṣa is in the throat region
śa is in the heart
items.inference: The syllables are mapped to throat and heart.
uncertainties: whether tadā indicates sequence or emphasis
items.plain_english: The syllable ṣa is in the throat region, and the syllable śa is in the heart.

items.question: What is declared about the places and wheels, and what should be heard?
premises: sthāna cakrāḥ tu saṃproktāḥ teṣāṃ dhyānaṃ śṛṇu priye
places and wheels are declared
their meditation should be heard
items.inference: The places and wheels are declared, and their meditation is to be heard, O beloved.
uncertainties: whether sthāna and cakrāḥ are separate or compound
items.plain_english: The places and wheels are declared; hear their meditation, O beloved.

items.question: How is the divine lotus described in this first octad?
premises: aṣṭa āraṃ paṅkajaṃ divyaṃ prathama aṣṭaka bhūṣitam
the lotus is eight-spoked and divine
it is adorned by the first octad
items.inference: The divine lotus is eight-spoked and adorned by the first octad.
uncertainties: whether prathama modifies aṣṭaka or the whole phrase
items.plain_english: The divine eight-spoked lotus is adorned by the first octad.

items.question: What should an equal-minded practitioner abandon through practice?
premises: abhyāsāt sama cittaḥ tu grāma dharmañ ca varjayet
through practice the mind becomes equal
village dharma should be abandoned
items.inference: Through practice, with equal mind, one should abandon village dharma.
uncertainties: whether grāma dharmañ is a compound
items.plain_english: Through practice, with equal mind, one should abandon village dharma.

items.question: What distant hearing and knowledge are linked with bond and paralysis?
premises: dūra āśravaṇa vijñānaṃ pāśa stobham tathā priye
distant hearing and knowledge are mentioned
bond and paralysis are likewise mentioned
items.inference: Distant hearing and knowledge are connected with bond and paralysis, O beloved.
uncertainties: exact syntactic grouping
items.plain_english: Distant hearing and knowledge, bond and paralysis, likewise, O beloved.

items.question: What is briefly said about immortality and transformation?
premises: amaratvam tathā devi samāsāt parivartanam
immortality and transformation are mentioned
the statement is brief
items.inference: Immortality and transformation are briefly stated, O goddess.
uncertainties: whether parivartanam modifies amaratvam
items.plain_english: Immortality and transformation, in brief, O goddess.

items.question: How is the second eight-petaled wheel described?
premises: dvitīyam aṣṭa patram tu teja dhyāna sudīpitam
the second eight-petaled wheel is mentioned
it is well illuminated by fire meditation
items.inference: The second eight-petaled wheel is well illuminated by fire meditation.
uncertainties: whether teja dhyāna is compound
items.plain_english: The second eight-petaled wheel is well illuminated by fire meditation.

items.question: What does one make in many ways when the mind is one-pointed in meditation?
premises: kurute bahudhā rūpaṃ dhyāna eka gata cetasaḥ
form is made in many ways
the mind is one-pointed in meditation
items.inference: One makes form in many ways when the mind is one-pointed in meditation.
uncertainties: whether cetasaḥ modifies rūpaṃ or dhyāna
items.plain_english: One makes form in many ways when the mind is one-pointed in meditation.

items.question: What does the angry one destroy in the triple world?
premises: kruddhaḥ tu saṃharet sarvaṃ trailokyaṃ sa cara acaram
when angry he destroys all
the triple world includes moving and unmoving
items.inference: When angry, he destroys all in the triple world, moving and unmoving.
uncertainties: whether sa cara acaram is a compound
items.plain_english: When angry, he destroys all in the triple world, moving and unmoving.

items.question: What is the third great wheel said to liberate?
premises: tṛtīyam tu mahā cakraṃ nava tattva pramocakaḥ
the third great wheel is mentioned
it liberates nine tattvas
items.inference: The third great wheel liberates the nine tattvas.
uncertainties: whether nava tattva is compound
items.plain_english: The third great wheel liberates the nine tattvas.

items.question: What destruction and seeing are mentioned from very far?
premises: balī palita nāśam tu sudūrāt darśanam tathā
wrinkle and grey hair destruction is mentioned
seeing from very far is likewise mentioned
items.inference: Destruction of wrinkles and grey hair, and seeing from very far, are mentioned.
uncertainties: exact syntactic grouping
items.plain_english: Destruction of wrinkles and grey hair, and seeing from very far, likewise.

items.question: What should one make in solitude while intent on meditation?
premises: ekānte bahudhā rūpaṃ kuru dhyānañ ca tatparaḥ
in solitude one should make form in many ways
one should be intent on meditation
items.inference: In solitude, one should make form in many ways and be intent on meditation.
uncertainties: whether dhyānañ is object of kuru or separate
items.plain_english: In solitude, make form in many ways and be intent on meditation.

items.question: What does constant practice make when one is intent?
premises: kurute amaratvaṃ hi satata abhyāsa tatparaḥ
immortality is made
constant practice with intent is the means
items.inference: Constant practice makes immortality when one is intent.
uncertainties: whether tatparaḥ modifies abhyāsa or subject
items.plain_english: Indeed, constant practice makes immortality when one is intent.

items.question: What will go through non-eating by day?
premises: divasāt nāśanena eva vayo mṛtyuṃ gamiṣyate
non-eating by day is the means
age and death will go
items.inference: Through non-eating by day, age and death will go.
uncertainties: whether vayo and mṛtyuṃ are separate objects
items.plain_english: Through non-eating by day, age and death will go.

items.question: What form results from constant practice of yoga for sixteen years?
premises: satata abhyāsa yogena dvi aṣṭa varṣa ākṛtiḥ bhavet
constant practice of yoga is the means
sixteen years yields a form
items.inference: Through constant practice of yoga for sixteen years, one becomes a form.
uncertainties: whether dvi aṣṭa means sixteen
items.plain_english: Through constant practice of yoga for sixteen years, one becomes a form.

items.question: What happens when one always contemplates smoke-colored form?
premises: dhūmra varṇaṃ sadā cintya trailokyaṃ cālayet priye
smoke-colored form is always contemplated
the triple world is shaken
items.inference: By always contemplating smoke-colored form, one shakes the triple world, O beloved.
uncertainties: whether dhūmra varṇaṃ is compound
items.plain_english: Always contemplate smoke-colored form; it shakes the triple world, O beloved.
